subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit `/new`/`/reset` and automatic daily/idle rollovers, and what blocking/background/config/security boundaries should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior affects reset latency, silent tool execution, durable memory retention, plugin contracts, config defaults, and privacy/security policy.

options.title: Define bounded pre-reset flush
options.body: Approve explicit policy for manual, daily, and idle resets with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, sandbox/tool constraints, and no duplicate session-memory hook behavior.

options.title: Keep reset persistence mechanical
options.body: Treat hook/session-memory improvements such as #61675 as the supported reset boundary and narrow or decline silent reset-time agent execution.

options.title: Defer to memory plugins
options.body: Require continuous persistence or external memory plugins to own curated memory while core only extends lifecycle events where current plugin APIs are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Define bounded pre-reset flush
recommendation.body: Approve explicit policy for manual, daily, and idle resets with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, sandbox/tool constraints, and no duplicate session-memory hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the pre-compaction flush primitive and `/new` reset history, making them the best available owner for the cross-boundary decision.
